To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the co-occurrence method outperformed the dictionary-based method for phrasal translation in the English–Chinese CLIR task; and (2) pre- and post-translation query expansion techniques slightly improved performance in the English– Chinese CLIR task.

(1) the use of phrasal translation can significantly improve CLIR performance; (2) co-occurrence information can be used to help identify phrasal translation candidates; and (3) query expansion can improve CLIR performance.
(a) co-occurrence based phrasal translation is a promising approach for CLIR on Web data, and (b) pre- and post-translation query expansion can improve the performance of CLIR on Web portals.
